slides.title: Health & Safety Starts with Noticing
slides.content: Most accidents do not happen because someone deliberately breaks the rules. They happen because people stop noticing: Hazards become "normal". People are rushing. People are distracted. People do not want to make a fuss. Good safety starts by paying attention to your surroundings.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Health & Safety Starts with Noticing'? Select all that apply.
options: People do not want to make a fuss
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Health & Safety Starts with Noticing.

slides.title: What Switches Noticing Off
slides.content: Common causes include: Rushing. Thinking "it's always been like that." Phones and other distractions. Not wanting to speak up. Good habits include: Asking "Is this normal?" Saying concerns out loud. Treating near misses as learning opportunities.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'What Switches Noticing Off'?
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on What Switches Noticing Off.

slides.title: Safety Basics Everyone Must Know
slides.content: You should know: Your fire exit route. Your assembly point. Who to tell if something is wrong. That walkways and fire exits must stay clear. PPE rules must always be followed when required.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Safety Basics Everyone Must Know'? Select all that apply.
options: Who to tell if something is wrong
That walkways and fire exits must stay clear
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Safety Basics Everyone Must Know.

slides.title: Reporting Problems Is Part of Safety
slides.content: Tell your teacher if you notice: Hazards. Near misses. Damaged equipment. Facilities issues. Something unsafe. Reporting is not making a fuss. It is helping keep everyone safe.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Reporting Problems Is Part of Safety'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Reporting Problems Is Part of Safety.

slides.title: Show Respect
slides.content: Health and safety is linked to the PROUD value of Show Respect. Respect means: For the Space: Tidy up. Report damage. Leave things as you found them. For Other People: Do not interfere with their equipment. Do not create unnecessary risks. For Staff: Respect safety decisions and instructions.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'Show Respect'? Select all that apply.
options: Leave things as you found them
Do not interfere with their equipment
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on Show Respect.

slides.title: Media & Studio Safety
slides.content: Important subject-specific rules include: Closed-toe shoes in studios. Use sandbags on lighting stands. Use camera wrist straps. Secure tripods correctly. Store cables properly. Complete risk assessments before location shoots. Return equipment after use. These are industry-standard expectations.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'Media & Studio Safety'?
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on Media & Studio Safety.

slides.title: Responsibility Is Shared
slides.content: Your responsibilities include: Using equipment safely. Returning equipment. Reporting faults. Following procedures. College responsibilities include: Equipment testing. Building maintenance. Electrical safety. Health and safety systems.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following is a key point about 'Responsibility Is Shared'?
exercise.explanation: This is a key point from the section on Responsibility Is Shared.

slides.title: If Something Feels Unsafe
slides.content: Safety is not only about physical hazards. You should speak up if: A space feels unsafe. An activity feels unsafe. Someone's behaviour makes you uncomfortable. Tell someone early.

exercise.prompt: Which of the following are mentioned in 'If Something Feels Unsafe'? Select all that apply.
exercise.explanation: All of these are covered in the section on If Something Feels Unsafe.

slides.title: Quick Revision Summary
slides.content: Key points to remember: Safety starts with noticing Report hazards early Respect people, spaces and equipment Follow studio safety procedures Know evacuation and reporting processes
